changes: 3.18.2: the long checks the owner asked for, as tools. tests/soak.mjs (npm run soak): an Endless run with a bot (default 90 waves; the live loop and renderer) sampled every third wave: the JS heap, geometries, textures, programs and objects of the scene, the DOM, the music voices and the lists of the world; the first third is warm-up, from the middle to the last third nothing may keep growing (the floor of the geometries, programs and objects is compared: they depend on the biome of the moment); a step that does not answer in a minute stops the page with the debugger and prints the stack, a crash of the page is a finding. Measured: the heap stays at 11 MB over 120 waves (flame), geometries and programs plateau (150 to 250 and 24 to 27), 7 weapons. tests/fuzz.mjs (npm run fuzz): a seeded monkey (clicks any visible control, keys, runs, pauses, resizes, dialogs) over five window sizes, checking for page errors, dead screens, an unreadable save and the layout audit every 20 steps; 7 seeds with 1000 steps each pass. It found that the layout audit counted buttons under a dialog or another screen on top as covered (by design); fixed in the audit. tests/balance.mjs (npm run balance): how far a plain mortal bot gets and, in god mode, how many seconds each weapon needs for an ordinary wave and a boss wave (24 to 37 s and 19 to 43 s: no weapon is out of line; the mortal bot dies at the first boss with every weapon, so it says little about weapons). Found by reading the browser log of a soak run: a tine of the Blackout City electric piano (7.1 times the pitch of a note in the high octave) lay at 24992 Hz, above the limit of the sampling rate (the browser clamped it and warned); it is left out above 16 kHz, and the deep test now fails when any sound or track asks for a tone outside 15 Hz to 20 kHz (all 310 sounds and ten tracks). RL_NO_MINIFY=1 node build.js builds a readable bundle. Not found: any leak. Known and not ours: the headless Chromium of the test machine sometimes crashes in a long soak run (its GPU process logs errors; the heap of the game is flat).

3.18.1: the old track no longer rings on under the new one (the owner heard the normal music under the boss music, and he was right). A track change used to cut only the notes that were still to come; the pads and bells already sounding (some for several seconds), the echoes of the delay line and the tail of the room played on. SoundEngine.quietOld now runs at every track change: the sounding music voices fade out over 0.25 s, the echo line gets no feedback for 0.7 s while it empties, and the music reverb is swapped for a fresh convolver (the old one fades out and is disconnected). Measured in the deep test (trackSwitch, 4 tracks, offline render): without the cut 8 to 40 % of the level of the track is still heard 0.3 to 1.75 s after the change, with it about 1 %. Not changed: the calm motif that the boss tracks carry on purpose (the owner chose the fade-out only). Also: the deploy of 3.17.2 failed on GitHub because a threshold of the deep test (calm Ember Works / Void Core rhythm 0.099 against 0.1) lay inside the noise of the test itself: the music renders of the test are seeded now, and the impulse of the music reverb and the pink and brown noise are made from their own seeded generator instead of Math.random at first use (the same kind of noise); two uncached runs give identical numbers.

3.18.0: always landscape (owner request: remove the "turn your phone" screen, like Clash of Clans or Brawl Stars). On a phone or tablet held upright, a small shell in the head of index.html writes the same page into a frame (?frame=1) that is as wide as the screen is tall and turned by 90 degrees (translateX + rotate), so the game always sees a landscape screen; the safe-area insets are remapped to the turned sides (--st/--sr/--sb/--sl). It re-fits on resize, orientationchange and visual viewport changes; a run no longer pauses when the phone is turned. The rotate screen, its CSS and the needsRotate pause logic are gone; screen.orientation.lock stays for installed apps. The shell replaces its own document in a task of its own (document.open does nothing while the parser runs a script of the page, found by testing); inside the frame the touch sticks listen to pointermove instead of pointerrawupdate, whose coordinates come without the turn of the frame (the stick moved the wrong way; found by testing), and read the position of the event itself. Desktop and automated browsers run the game directly (?shell=1 forces the shell, ?shell=0 disables it; window.__rlShell tells). Tests: full-qa shell section (upright phone: frame turned and fitted, the game sees landscape, no rotate screen, a run goes on, a tall desktop window has no frame), layout360 adapted.

3.17.2: sound notes, a way to tune the sound by ear with the player instead of describing it in words (the owner found the Music Lab mixer of an earlier branch not good). The sound engine remembers the sounds of the last half minute (SoundEngine.heard: one entry per distinct sound such as step:ice, eshot:warden or place:siren, counted, updated in place, at most 80) and the music that plays now (musicNow). The pause menu and the settings of the main menu have a Sound notes button: a list of what was heard lately (the music first, the clicks of the menu itself left out), a tap on one shows the reasons (too loud, too quiet, harsh, muddy, boring, repetitive, doesn't fit, love it), a tap on a reason saves a note with the sound, the reason, the wave, the biome and the music; Copy notes puts all of them in one text to send; Clear removes them. The notes live in localStorage under riftline.soundNotes (the last 300), not in the save. Back and Esc lead to where the notes were opened. Tests: self-test v3172 (counts, distinct sounds, order, the bound, the music), full QA soundnotes-desktop and -phone (the flow in the pause menu and from the settings, the saved note, the copied text, Back, Esc, Clear).

3.17.1: optimisation, no change for players (measured first: the simulation costs 0.16 ms a step in a busy Endless wave and a frame is 59 to 108 draw calls and 15 to 21 thousand triangles, so those stay as they are). The build splits src/build-info.json: the game fetches build-info.json at every start (the health check, the update handshake) and reads only the version and the build id from it, but it carried the whole changelog (93 % of 50 KB, four KB more with every release); dist/build-info.json is now the 0.4 KB identity file and dist/changes.json holds the history (nothing fetches it); src/build-info.json stays the one place the release notes are written. The five app icons are recompressed losslessly (every pixel identical, 383 KB to 333 KB, the two 512 px ones cached at install). Faster tests: the sections of the full QA that only look at state and the DOM no longer let the browser draw the 3D scene (the draw calls are no-ops, everything else runs: the simulation, the renderer's own code, the shaders, the DOM); the sections that take screenshots draw for real, and so do the E2E, the screenshots and the audits (QA_DRAW=1 draws everywhere). Not done on purpose: lazy-loading the 77 KB self-test (it needs ES-module chunks instead of the single-file IIFE and an asynchronous health check for the gain of about 20 KB gzipped), and cheaper reverbs (they would change the sound).

3.17.0: the walker (roadmap section 2, decided with the owner on 03.10.2026: two legs, not four). The drone is a two-legged robot (render/models.js buildPlayerModel): a squat torso with a glowing visor and a back pack, a pelvis, two legs of thigh, shin and a flat foot with glow strips in the weapon colour, the weapon mount on top; the footprint, the hull colours and the weapon-colour glow are the same as before. The legs follow the stride of the world (core/walk.js: player.stride is the metres walked; a foot comes down every metre, alternating): the thigh swings, the knee bends while the leg swings forward, the torso turns against the hips, the body bobs and leans into the movement; standing, it breathes (also in the start screen preview). A dash is a jump: the legs tuck, the body rises and falls over the 0.17 s, a `land` event comes when it ends (a ring, a burst of what the ground is made of and a small shake). Every step is a `step` event with the ground under the foot: the floor of the biome (wet asphalt in Blackout City, steel grating in the Ember Works, frozen ground in the Cryo Vault, mud in the Toxin Marsh, glass in the Void Core), or ice where the drone stands on a sheet, or acid in a pool. Sounds: a footstep per ground (a soft slap with the odd splash, a clank with an inharmonic ring, a crunch of three grains, a glassy scrape, a squelch with a bubble, a glass tick, a sizzling splash), a faint servo whine in each, the landing the same, heavier, with a thump; each foot is panned a little to its side, up to six steps a second, quiet (under 60 % of a Pulse shot, tested). The exhaust flames and the trail of the old hull are gone. Tests: self-test v3170 (no steps standing, a step per metre, alternating feet, none in the air, one landing, the ground of every biome, ice and acid, the model's legs swing opposite, tuck in the air, stand on the floor), deep test (the footsteps differ from each other, the level limit), attack shots (walker-1-stand, -2-stride, -3-jump).

3.16.0: every boss attack with a look and sound of its own (found by checking 3.10.0 again after the owner noticed that the Warden still had its old attacks): the Warden, Hive Queen and Rift Core fired the generic orb; now the Warden fires siren slugs (a capsule that flashes red and blue), the Hive Queen thorny toxic spores, the Rift Core upright rift rings (World.shoot gives a boss's shots its kind). The Warden's laser grid uses the security laser of Blackout City, the Rift Core's turning beams the rift ribbon (the warnings stay red). The Warden's charge cracks the wall it hits (the look and sound of its stomp). Every boss volley sounds, with a voice per boss (siren crack, wet spit, glassy rift pulse, crystal chime, slag glob); several spirals and rings flew silently. The weaver and the carrier have shot voices of their own. Searing Collapse leaves burning ground for 3 s. Self-test v3160 (every boss through 70 s of its fight with its Overdrive: no orb, no beam without skin or colour, every volley names its boss; the burning ground). Also everything else the requests since 03.10.2026 promised and the earlier releases left out (a check of all of them): the portals a boss calls open (summons, reinforcements) wear the boss's colours with a turning sigil; the sentinel's beam is the security laser in Blackout City and the rift ribbon in the Void Core; sounds of the props near the drone (3.13.0 plan): street lamps buzz along the edges of Blackout City, the machine blocks of the Ember Works carry a turning gear that is heard, the obelisks of the Void Core hum; the Cryo Vault calm theme keeps time with its place as it swells (icicles on the off-beats, ice creaks on 2 and 4, a gust every fourth bar) and the boss tracks of the Frost Prism, Hive Queen and Rift Core take their place into the drums (an ice crack on the clap and falling icicles, frogs on the hand drums and bubbles on the ghosts, glitches and a reversed swell) (3.14.0 plan). New tests: the prop sounds near and far, the boss portals, the sentinel's skin (v3160); the boss drums and the Cryo Vault rhythm (deep test placeMusic); the ambience of every biome stays below 60 % of the level of its calm theme (deep test ambience; measured 5 to 33 %).

3.15.0: boss rewards (core/boss-cards.js). Every boss has an exclusive card (rarity 6, "Boss", a crimson card with a gold rim and the boss seal), offered only after its kill: 30 % chance on its own random stream, +15 % after each boss offer without one, back to 30 % when one comes; it takes the first place of the offer and stays there through a reroll; at most once per run (owned cards never come again, also in Endless); the chance is saved with the run. The cards: Lockdown Grid (Warden; every 8 s a gold laser cage of six pylons drops on the densest group, holds it for 3 s and burns it), Crucible Hammer (Crucible; every 6 s the next dash ends in a slam, 75 damage, fire and molten ground for 3 s), Shard Field (Frost Prism; kills shatter into 5 ice splinters that hit and chill), Brood (Hive Queen; every 10 kills a larva hatches, up to 4, hunts an enemy and bursts into poison), Event Collapse (Rift Core; the Nova pulls everything in for 0.35 s, then blasts 40 % harder). Each with a model, sounds, effects and a self-test (v3150); their own damage sources in the run summary; codex entries say which boss gives them.

3.14.0: music of the place (option a of the owner: keep melody and key, the place brings rhythm and instruments): the calm themes keep their motif, pad and sub and add the rhythm of their place as the intensity rises: Blackout City noir (a walking bass on every beat over root, fifth, third and a step to the next chord; brushes on 2 and 4 and light taps; the far siren on the chord), Ember Works industrial (a piston on the beats, a conveyor in sixteenths, a hammer on 4), Toxin Marsh bayou (a log drum on root and fifth in a lazy syncopation, the frogs croak in time on the and of 2 and 4), Void Core (a choir at the head of every fourth bar, glitches in time at the end of every second bar); the Cryo Vault stays the model. The boss tracks already carry their places (anvils, the siren). Where the calm theme plays a sound of the place (rain drops, crickets, the heartbeat), the bed of that sound steps back to half. Deep test: each rhythm comes in between intensity 0.1 and 0.9; self-test v3140 (the bed steps back only under the calm theme); node tools/qa.js scape-preview music renders all ten tracks to MP3.

3.13.0: soundscapes (audio/place.js SCAPE): every biome has a steady layer of soft grains (Blackout City light rain as single drops, gutters and rain on metal, no hiss; Ember Works the low roar of the furnaces; Cryo Vault wind through a narrow band; Toxin Marsh crickets; Void Core the heartbeat of the core) and 7 to 9 far sounds, each on its own timer (thunder every 25-50 s, a siren every 60-120 s, a helicopter every 70-140 s …; 21 new sounds: siren, helicopter, horn, dog, anvil series, drop hammer, conveyor, steam whistle, chain hoist, molten pour, howl, avalanche, crystals, frog chorus, cicadas, an insect flying past, splash, heron, a reversed swell, a metallic resonance, chirps): never two far sounds within 2.5 s, never the same twice in a row, two big ones at least 4 s apart, half as many in a boss fight (and a softer bed). Thunder comes with lightning over the arena, a passing siren with red and blue glows at the side of the view (renderer.scapeLight, floor flashes, no new lights). Levels locked in the deep test: the steady layers under 60 % of a Pulse shot, every other sound of the place under a Scattergun shot. Self-test v3130 (20 minutes per biome: rates, gaps, repeats, big ones, the bed, the lights, thinner boss fights); tests/scape-preview.mjs renders each biome to WAV/MP3.

3.12.0: the Singularity replaces the grenade ("you gotta get so close until they actually fly into the enemies that you'll basically always have defeated them already"): thrown fast and far (to the aim, 11 m, or the densest group in sight within 16 m; never into a wall), it opens a small rift that pulls the enemies around it together for 1.5 s (bosses stand, elites and big ones are pulled less, enemies in it walk slower), then collapses in a blast (90 x damage x Event Horizon, a short knock, a slow; Searing Collapse sets them on fire). Its own model (a dark core in two crossed rings with a cyan rim), flight with a trail and a landing marker, a pull with five spiral arms, a dark pool, a rim that snaps in before the collapse and sparks drawn inward, a collapse with an inward ring, a violet shock ring and a rift scar; three voices (singThrow, singPull, singCollapse). The cards keep their ids with new names (Rift Cells, Event Horizon, Searing Collapse), the gadget button is violet with a new icon, damage is still credited to the old id so run records stay readable. Self-test of the throw, the reach, the pull, elites, the collapse, walls and the cards; screenshots of the pull and the collapse.

3.11.0: landscape only on phones and tablets: the manifest asks for landscape (the installed app opens sideways), a run start tries screen.orientation.lock where the browser allows it, and a touch device held upright gets a rotate screen over everything (a turning phone, "Turn your device") while a run waits paused behind it (Esc does not resume it there); desktop windows of any shape keep working. The portrait-only layouts of phones and tablets (menu, upgrade choice, biome and boss cards) and the orientation chip of the button editor are gone; saved portrait layouts stay readable but are not used. Tests: the touch sections of the QA run on a landscape phone, a new rotate section, the button editor in landscape, the small phone at 640x360; the portrait E2E device and the portrait screenshots are gone.

3.10.0: the attacks of enemies and bosses look and sound like what they are (render/attacks-view.js); until 3.9.0 every zone of world.hazards was the same red ring around a flat red disc, every blast the same burst and sound, every mark on the floor a black blob and every enemy shot a glowing ball: now the zones have a surface of their kind (the Warden's stomp and the driller's blast crack the ground, the Crucible's hammer cracks it with lava seams, slag rings, eruptions and slag lobs well up as molten pools, the Frost Prism's nova and glaciers frost over from the rim, the Hive Queen's plague wells up as acid, the Rift Core's bombardments tear violet rifts, mortar shells, mines and charges get a turning target with a countdown sweep, burning and volatile ground smoulders), shared kinds take the look of their maker (the boom event carries src); the warning ring and the filling ring stay (yellow with Clear warnings); mines and sapper charges have models that blink faster, mortar shells fly as shells and the Crucible lobs glowing slag; the blasts differ (cracks with dust and lumps, pillars of fire, ice spikes that burst up and shatter, splashes of acid, bolts of light, fireballs with smoke) and each has a sound of its own (aQuake, aLava, aIce, aAcid, aRift, aFire); marks of the place replace the black blob of every blast and kill (burnt wet asphalt, glowing cracks that cool, melted frost with a star of new frost, a splash of mud with glowing slime, a violet scar), slag cools to a crust, frost melts, the marks of a biome go with it; enemy shots have shapes of their kind (Prism ice and weaver crystals, needles and homing pods as darts, tracers, lumps of slag) Tests: npm run check (quick) and npm run release-check (the whole chain with a time per step); waits that depend on the game count game time (the boss kill → upgrade choice check failed at random under software WebGL on main too); a QA section that throws closes its pages; the choice-screen sections reach the choice in one go and the workshop check waits for each purchase; the deep test reuses its sound results while the sound engine is unchanged (the chain: 51 → about 41-44 min, npm run check about 2 min).

3.9.0: sounds of the place (audio/place.js): the hazards sound where they are, panned and softer with the distance (lava vents bubble and draw a rising rumble and roar before they erupt; live manholes hum when you are close and crackle faster and faster with a rising whine while they charge; the ice cracks and creaks under the moving drone and sheets tinkle; acid pools bubble and the drone sizzles in acid; portals hum with two beating tones and whisper), and every biome has rare far sounds of its own every 5 to 11 s (Blackout City thunder, a car alarm, a passing car, police radio, sparks; Ember Works an anvil, chains, a steam valve, a conveyor; Cryo Vault an ice crack with a boom, icicles, a gust, the glacier's groan; Toxin Marsh frogs, a bird, an owl, mud; Void Core a deep swell, a glass shimmer, a breath, a glitch); pink and brown noise only, mostly tones; they are low-priority voices on a new ambience bus, which also carries the event beds and scales the atmospheres of the music; Settings > Ambience sets its volume (default 0.8, the level the atmospheres had)

3.8.0: the map hazards have models of their own instead of discs and rings (render/hazards-view.js): lava vents are basalt craters around a pool of lava under a drifting crust whose seams widen with the heat, a dome of lava swells while they warn and they erupt as a pillar of fire (a flame shader on a tube, no more glowing box column); live manholes are iron covers with a raised grid in a concrete collar that rattle, lift and leak a cold light while they charge and jump on jagged bolts when they arc; ice sheets are frozen sheets with frost streaks, fine cracks, facets and glints, with ice shards leaning out of the rim; acid pools are murky liquid with ripples, bubbles and foam (cyan for the Acid Coating) behind a bank of mud lumps and dead reeds; portals are turning swirls with a dark core and five rune stones floating around them; the warning rings stay; the Left-handed and Reduce flashes settings are removed (with their code: the mirrored touch halves and button layout, the softer light bursts); a save that has them drops them on load

3.7.1: fixes from a checkup: entering Endless reset the run clock but not the time of the last dash, so with Cryo Skates the dash could stay locked for as long as the run had lasted (World.restartClock moves the stamp with the clock); a hazard tick (acid) keeps its fraction until it adds up to a whole point, so a resistance works exactly and a tick that does no damage no longer counts as a hit (it sounded, shook the camera, flashed red and fed Heat Sink); a trap strike that misses (dash, shield, the moment of safety after a hit) no longer chills or stuns; the electric plate and the rift burst stun with their own sparks, flash and zap (event stun, HUD chip STUNNED) instead of the frost sparkle and ping of chill

3.7.0: the music has no loud noise any more: the atmospheres were a one-second loop of white noise (on a phone speaker up to three quarters of what one heard of a calm theme); now they are a soft bed of pink or brown noise well below the music, and the sounds of the place are notes of the calm themes (rain drops and gutter drips, embers, crickets, ice; the wind of the Cryo Vault sings on the chord); event ambiences too; the boss tracks are cinematic synth instead of metal (taikos, strings, brass, a choir, arpeggios, a pumping sub; no guitars, no cymbals), one style per boss: The Warden a cyberpunk chase (128 BPM), The Crucible forge drums and brass (104), Frost Prism ice trance (138), Hive Queen tribal acid (116), Rift Core drum and bass with a choir that quotes the motifs of the other biomes (172); each keeps the motif of its biome; a boss starts with a deep taiko, brass and choir and ends on a victory chord; the distortion bus and the guitar amps are gone; with the fixes of the 3.6.0 review that came after its merge: left-handed play mirrors only DASH, NOVA, GADGET and the fixed stick (not pause), a tap in the editor only selects, a cancelled drag snaps back, P no longer closes the editor, the readouts keep room for what a run adds, a layout that does not fit the screen falls back to the default with a note, Cryo Skates on ice keep the 0.8 s dash floor, and the Combo Surge sound rises per surge and ducks the music

3.6.0: a button layout editor (Settings > Button layout) over the real HUD: DASH, NOVA, GADGET and pause are dragged to any free spot of the safe area and resized (60 to 160 %), with an opacity for the buttons, a stick size for both sticks and a fixed move stick that can be placed on the move side; places that cover another control or the hull, wave, shard or boss readouts are refused; portrait and landscape keep their own layouts, left-handed play mirrors them; Esc or Cancel leave without saving; checkup fixes: the dash cooldown never drops below 0.8 s, every Orbital Blade has its own cooldown per enemy, Combo Surge has its own shockwave look and sound, Toxin Marsh acid pools are smaller and a darker green, the upgrade choice on portrait phones sits in the middle without a gap above REROLL and keeps values and units together, Saver draws without edge smoothing (from the next start) and the overlay at one pixel per CSS pixel

3.5.0: the calm themes of all biomes follow the Cryo Vault (no beat until the intensity is high, a motif of struck notes in the echo and the room, a soft pad, a deep sub, sounds of the place) with an instrument of their own: Blackout City an electric piano, Ember Works struck pipes, Toxin Marsh a kalimba, Void Core glass; slower tempos (60 to 78 BPM); the boss tracks lay the motif of their biome and its pad over the drums and guitars so they sound like the same place at its darkest; the music voice budget is 44

3.4.0: Blackout City replaces the Neon Yard (id yard kept for saves): wet black asphalt with puddles, rain rings and worn yellow road markings, jersey barriers with reflectors, advertising columns, wrecked cars and dumpsters, a skyline of dark towers with few lit windows and aircraft lights, street lamps, traffic lights, steaming manholes, rain; enemies look rain-wet with red and blue emergency light on their rims; the Warden (Enforcer of the Blackout) carries a turning police light bar

3.4.0: live manholes as the hazard of Blackout City (the vent mechanic with an electric skin: they crackle, then arc in thin flickering bolts; the current hurts and stuns enemies); a new biome event BLACKOUT (the light fades out, three more manholes arc in a chain around the arena, shards +25%) with its own cue and ambience; armed gangs in the enemy mix (gunner, bomber, grunt), the first visit keeps the global unlock order

3.4.0: new music for Blackout City: noir trip-hop in the rain (92 BPM, walking bass, electric piano, muted trumpet, siren, thunder, radio chatter) and a darksynth boss track (128 BPM, four on the floor, rolling distorted bass, double-tracked guitars, siren lead, helicopter); the Music block in Settings shows the current tempos (they were still those of 3.1.0); the electric plate and the laser traps take the city's colours

3.3.0: harder bosses: every boss after the first has a quarter more hull per boss before it (at most double) and rests less between attacks; enraged, it adds an Overdrive attack to its pattern (Warden laser lockdown grid, Crucible expanding lava rings with gaps, Prism three-beam whiteout with homing shards, Queen acid plague, Core collapse under a beam cross); Warden, Crucible and Prism call biome reinforcements through telegraphed portals; bigger escorts; floor traps on boss waves from wave 15

3.3.0: Endless mutators: from wave 21 every tenth wave adds one for the rest of the run, in a seeded order (Volatile: enemies may burst when they die; Shielded: may carry a shield; Hasted; Armored; Barrage: faster, harder shots; Trap Storm: more traps, shorter pauses); once all six are in play they level up to III; announced after the biome card with a banner and a cue, shown as HUD chips

3.2.0: boss tracks rebuilt and much harder: double-tracked guitars through two amp chains (drive, tight low cut, mid scoop, cabinet), metal kicks with a beater click, blast beats, breakdowns with the kick in unison with the guitars, a kick that pumps pads, bass and guitars, a room reverb, a glue compressor, and many noises of the biome (Yard breakcore with reese, acid and vocal chops; Works gallop riffs, anvils, hydraulics; Vault black-metal tremolo and ice bells; Marsh sludge wobble and squelches; Void tritone riffs, glitches and drones)

3.2.0: calm themes calmer and atmospheric, over a loop of their place: wind and gusts in the Cryo Vault, insects and murk in the Toxin Marsh, furnace and far machines in the Ember Works, rain and city hum in the Neon Yard, beating drones and space wind in the Void Core; slower tempos (66 to 96 BPM)
3.2.0: sounds are panned by where they happen (left or right of the drone) and big blasts ring out in a room whose size follows the biome; pausing keeps the place of the music
3.1.0: What's new tab on the home screen (News) with short notes for the latest versions; a dot marks it until it was opened once per version

3.1.0: new music — every biome has its own calm theme with a rhythm of its own and sounds that belong to the place (Neon Yard synthwave stomp with transformer hum, neon flicker, sirens and data blips; Ember Works industrial stomp with anvil hits, clangs, gear and chain ratchets, steam and furnace rumble; Cryo Vault sparse and cold with wind, ice cracks and wind chimes; Toxin Marsh swung dub with bubbles, frog croaks, insects and mud squelches; Void Core broken odd-grouped beat with drones, whispers and reversed swells), with fills and section changes so nothing repeats every four bars

3.1.0: heavy boss tracks — one hard instrumental track per biome in the key of its calm theme (Yard cyber-breakcore 175 BPM, Works industrial metal 150, Vault cold drum'n'bass 172, Marsh sludge/wobble 140, Void cosmic horror 160) with drop, variation, half-time breakdown and build; it starts exactly when the boss appears at the camera pan with a crash and impact, gets heavier on the boss' phase and enrage events and resolves into the calm theme when the boss dies
3.1.0: Settings has a Music block with a preview button per biome for the calm theme and the boss track

3.0.0: traps — from wave 6 the arena fights back, with a skin per biome: floor strikes (Neon Yard electric plate, Ember Works piston crusher, Cryo Vault ice spikes, Toxin Marsh acid geyser, Void rift burst), sweeping beams from wave 9 (laser, flame jet, rift beam) and mines from wave 12 (mine, frost mine, spore pod, rift mine). Each warns first (ring, line, blinking light), hurts you and, as a share of their hull, enemies; chill, acid puddles and knock-back as side effects. None on boss waves. In Endless there are about half as many more, pauses and warnings are shorter, floor strikes hunt you from wave 40 and beams cross

3.0.0: Grenade gadget (key G, a GADGET button on touch screens): two charges, about 6 s to recharge one, thrown where you aim or at the densest group in sight, never into a wall; blast with knock-back and a slow; new cards Grenade Cells, Blast Core and Incendiary Mix (55 upgrades)

3.0.0: burst cap and a steeper Endless — from wave 40 an enemy can lose only a shrinking share of its hull within a quarter of a second (12% from about wave 148), however many shots, pierces, explosions and chain jumps land; Nova and bosses are exempt; regular enemies get +3% hull per wave beyond wave 30. A maxed Railgun used to wipe whole lines at wave 150. Damage numbers now show single attacks instead of running totals

3.0.0: new looks and sounds for it all — a model per trap skin, grenade with arc, landing marker and blast, a spark for resisted hits; 26 new sounds (grenade throw and blast, resisted hit, trap warnings, beams and strikes per skin, mine fuses)

2.9.1: no more stuck run when every upgrade is maxed — the wave end used to open an empty upgrade choice (reported at wave ~150) and the run could not go on; now the choice is skipped, the hull is repaired by 35% and a few shards are paid ("ALL UPGRADES MAXED" toast), and a saved run stuck on the empty choice resumes into the next wave

2.9.1: Ember Jet sounds like a flame — it fired 15 short noise bursts a second, which ticked and clicked; every shot now starts a soft, overlapping, sustained burst (low rumble, airy hiss, rare soft crackle), tested for steady loudness

2.9.1: fixes — long noise bursts (rocket, flame, event beds) are no longer cut off after about half a second; instanced arena props free their GPU buffers when the arena changes; a restored WebGL context is announced; the Weaver now announces its shot (lock-on sound and 0.45 s of aiming after the warp) and the Drone paths around obstacles instead of getting stuck on them

2.9.0: more detail in the arenas — every biome gets a detail layer (two draw calls per biome, placed from the arena seed): tall backdrop props outside the border (Neon Yard towers, containers and floodlights; Works smokestacks, furnaces and cranes; Vault ice spires and frozen wrecks; Toxin Marsh dead trees, giant mushrooms and bone piles; Void floating islands and crystal spires) and flat decals inside (chevrons, grates, soot and gears, frost patches, puddles and lily pads, rune circles), never on the start area

2.9.0: more detail on enemies and bosses — all 25 enemy types get a second pass (panels, vents, rivets, lamps, pupils, teeth, claws, tails, glow cores; 240-460 triangles each, same footprint and draw calls); Crucible and Frost Prism get the detail level of Warden, Queen and Core

2.9.0: sound — seven clearly different weapon shots (bright pew, fat shotgun, electric crackle, heavy rail with a metal tail, rising rocket whoosh, spinning-blade shing, pitchless flame roar), nine enemy death families, own shots for drones, turrets and bosses, a signature timbre and motif per boss (telegraphs, enrage, death), louder and denser event beds, a different pick sound per upgrade rarity, and a short music duck (at most 15% for 80 ms) on big hits; the music never pauses and notes survive a sound flood (tested)

2.8.1: fixes — upgrade cards stay visible with reduced motion; no crash when the Whiteout snow fades after going home; two tabs or windows no longer overwrite each other's save; Endless keeps the screen awake and its summary counts only the Endless part; Restart and Run Again keep the weapon and threat of the run; starting a new run over a stored one credits its shards; UI feedback toasts stay visible in the pause menu; dialogs take and return focus and Esc closes them from a text field; a held stick survives small viewport changes; a hanging network falls back to the cached page after 3 s; at most three save backups; formatCount shows millions

2.8.1: gameplay fixes — a resumed wave keeps its supply caches and bonus group; Endless bosses start from the wave-20 hull and keep growing; Resonance chains only by chance on non-Tesla weapons; elite splitters' mites are not elites; bosses' leftover adds and kills after death pay nothing; Rebound only bounces to enemies in sight; Echo volleys do not shift Overload and Overdrive; Rebound and Tungsten Core are not offered where they do nothing; Repair Beacon heals inside its ring only; Sentinel walks up when it has no line of sight; Weaver stops shooting a dead player; the Queen stops summoning in a crowded arena
2.8.1: sound — the music no longer stutters or drops out in heavy fights (shots and hits used to take its voices; it now has its own voice budget)
2.8.1: smaller — empty instance pools are not drawn, safe-area insets are cached

2.8.0: upgrade offers — fewer commons, more rare cards: the card weights are now 42/32/20/6 for common/rare/epic/legendary (were 60/28/10/2), and an offer is never made of commons only (its last card becomes a rare or better one)

2.8.0: five weak or overlapping upgrades are gone and their levels move to the one they resembled (old saves and pending offers are converted): Long Barrel → Targeting Chip (now also +8% range and +6% projectile speed), Tractor Field → Supply Loop (the workshop Magnet Coil keeps the pickup radius), Vector Capacitor → Servo Thrusters (now also -8% dash and Aegis cooldown per level), Glass Core → High-Yield Rounds, Momentum Core → Rapid Cycler; 52 upgrades

2.8.0: stronger commons and weak rares — High-Yield Rounds +18%, Reinforced Hull +25 HP, Targeting Chip, Cryo Rounds 25%, Shock Dash 60/90, Overload (every 5th shot, 45+15 per level, bigger burst), Acid Coating 22%, Apex Hunter +15%

2.8.0: smarter auto-aim — enemies behind a wall are not targeted any more (shots would only hit the wall; only the Lance slug, which flies through walls, may aim through them), close enemies come first (under 4 m strongly), rushers that explode, ram or jump at you (Bomber, Charger, Striker, Leaper, Sapper) are preferred a bit earlier, enemies that are immune right now (shield phase) only when nothing else is in reach, and the current target is kept while it is still a good one so the aim does not flicker; the manual aim assist skips enemies behind walls too

2.7.0: new look — the player drone is an arrow-shaped gunship (canopy, swept wings with glowing strips, twin thrusters whose flame follows speed, leans and banks); all 25 enemy types have new silhouettes with one memorable feature each (biological ones rounder and asymmetric, machines with panels, vents and lights); Warden, Hive Queen and Rift Core got more detail

2.7.0: enemies move with life — walk sway, hops, leaning into the movement direction, breathing or hovering at rest, hit squash, a spawn pop and a short shrink-and-spin death with a second debris burst (skipped on the battery preset); no extra geometry or draw calls
2.7.0: stronger biome skins — thicker lava veins with glow, frost rim and glints, more slime, violet void cracks; warning colours of attacks are unchanged

2.7.0: own sounds — six death sound families over the 25 enemies, telegraph sounds for charge, aim, fuse, mine and lob, one intro motif per boss plus telegraphs, enrage, phase and boss-down sounds, a boss variant of each biome's music (faster, extra voice), ambience and a cue for every biome event, a pick sound per upgrade rarity, reroll, card hover and wave-clear sounds, and a quiet engine hum; mixed through a limiter with a voice limit
2.6.0: touch sticks stay where the finger touched down: the centre no longer follows the finger when it is dragged far (move and aim)
2.6.0: the camera pan to a new boss lasts 3 s (was 1.5 s), the boss warning banner 3 s, the biome title card 3.5 s of its wave (was 1.6 s); input is never blocked by the cards

2.6.0: upgrades rebalanced after a bot benchmark (wave 14, all weapons): weaker — Resonance (+1 chain jump every 2nd level, +6% chain), Payload blast 30%+10%/level, Overcharge (Nova +30%), Chrono Dash 1.5 s, Overdrive Pulse (every 5th shot, double damage), Cluster Payload (2 bomblets, less damage); Split Chamber and Rebound are Epic now; stronger — Reactive Plating (30+20 damage, -4% fire rate), Targeting Chip (+10% crit and +0.06 crit multiplier), Rapid Cycler +15%, Servo Thrusters +10%, Long Barrel +25%, Cryo Rounds 20%, Vector Capacitor -10%, Last Stand -22%, Shock Dash 40/64, Overload, Combo Surge (60/90), Orbital Blades 18, Phantom Dash -50%, Dragon's Breath

2.6.0: Capacitor Bank is part of Overcharge (each kill adds 1% Nova charge per level) and Bounty Protocol part of Supply Loop (elite kills drop +1 shard per level); levels in old saves and pending offers move over; 57 upgrades
2.6.0: the workshop module Salvager is called Shard Refinery (the run upgrade keeps the name Salvager Core); Bloodrush cards show their cap

2.5.1: code refactor, no change to the game: the patches of the content packs and later fixes (methods wrapped from outside, up to eight times each) are folded into the classes and functions, so every method is in one place
2.5.1: about 3,600 minified local names (t, e, n …) are readable names; the minifier's syntax tricks (!0, comma chains, a && f() as a statement, var) are plain statements
2.5.1: the deep self-test has its own module (core/selftest.js); window.__riftTest uses the real names; Prettier formats the code and CI checks it
2.5.1: the save-sanitize health check expected the old High-Yield maximum 8 and reported FAIL since 2.5.0; it reads the maximum from the upgrade now

2.5.0: upgrades without duplicates — 19 weaker copies are folded into the upgrade they copied (e.g. Overbore Caliber and Kinetic Matrix into High-Yield Rounds, Afterburner and Cryo Coolant into Vector Capacitor, which now also shortens the Aegis cooldown); the kept upgrades have higher maximums, so a build reaches about the same totals. 59 upgrades, 13 evolutions unchanged

2.5.0: six new upgrades with their own mechanic — Cryo Skates (faster on ice and in Cryo Vault), Acid Coating (hits leave your own cyan acid, enemies in it take +25%), Heat Sink (fire-rate burst and Nova charge near lava or acid), Slipstream (+25% damage after a dash), Combo Surge (longer combos, a shockwave every 15 combo kills), Reactive Plating (a hit releases a repulse wave, -8% fire rate)

2.5.0: workshop — Rift Battery and Reactor Core are merged into Nova Cell (4 levels, at least 25% Nova per level at the start of each wave), Route Scanner into Field Supply (+1 cache and +50% cache shards per level); bought levels of the removed modules are refunded in full

2.5.0: three new workshop modules — Starter Kit (a random common upgrade per level at the start of a run), Hazard Attunement (+10% damage and +0.5 HP/s near a map hazard per level), Emergency Shield (once per wave below 30% hull: a short barrier and a repair)

2.5.0: stronger biomes — about five hazards per wave instead of three, about 25–30% larger (vents 1.7–2.2, ice 2.7–3.7, acid 2.2–3.0), kept clear of obstacles and further from the spawn; Void Core has two portal pairs in most waves

2.5.0: biome events, one per visit of a hazard biome (waves 2–4 of the visit, never a boss wave, +25% shards): Meltdown (Ember Works, extra vents that erupt together), Whiteout (Cryo Vault, snow storm with dense fog and more ice), Spore Bloom (Toxin Marsh, pools grow and new ones sprout), Rift Storm (Void Core, portals jump to new spots, shown 1.6 s ahead)
2.5.0: the signature enemies of a biome can appear from its first wave (at half weight until their normal unlock wave); Neon Yard is unchanged
2.5.0: biome title card on wave 1 and every biome change (name, hazard, boss) and a boss intro card during the camera pan to a new boss
